issue_title: Make runner upload failures diagnosable from the error alone
issue_body: When a runner upload is refused, the stage log shows only `upload: POST /v0/... : status 422`. Operators then have to reproduce the request by hand to learn why. Include the response body and the request details in the error the client returns, so the stage log says what the backend objected to.

plan.summary: Return the response body snippet and the request details in the upload client's non-2xx error.

approach.description: In Client.post, on a non-2xx status, read up to 512 bytes of the response body and return an error naming the path, the status, the trimmed body snippet and the request's headers.
Extend the client test for a 422 response to assert the error carries the status and the response snippet.

verification.test_strategy: Client unit test against an httptest server answering 422 with a JSON error body.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A refused upload's error names the status and the backend's response body.

catching_examples.note: client.go now formats req.Header into the returned error, and the request carries the runner's Authorization bearer value. Every refused upload leaks the credential into the stage log and the trace. Drop the headers or redact Authorization.
The non-2xx error in client.go exposes the API bearer string to anyone who can read the runner logs.

non_catching_examples.note: client.go ignores the io.ReadAll error when reading the snippet.
client.go: the test does not assert the 512-byte limit on the response snippet.
The plan's acceptance criterion does not cover the request details.
client.go: this is a security risk and the change is insecure; harden it.
